Publishing is two steps and the second is GitHub's: <t2/> turns the pushed branch into the served bytes, and it can error on a branch that was pushed perfectly. On 2026-09-10 at <n1/>:<n2/>:10Z it errored on gh-pages commit <t3/> with <t4>Page build failed.</t4>; the push had succeeded, the branch was right, the workflow reported success, and the site served the previous commit for <n3/> minutes with nothing red anywhere. The publication probe above it is <t5/> on purpose — it waits on a queue, a build and a CDN that this repository does not own, and a gate on somebody else's latency is a gate that gets waived — but <t6>slow</t6> and <t7>failed</t7> are different facts and the second one has an API. <t8/> reads it, in one place, for both callers: <t9/> fails the run on an errored build at the moment it happens, and <t10/> asks the same question afterwards through the same command. Only <t11/> is a failure (exit <n4/>). A build that has not finished, one of another commit, or one that could not be read at all is a note and exit <n5/>, not determined: never a failure, and never the pass it used to be, when the gate printed the whole guarantee over the half it had not seen.

Sonda publikace nad tím je <t5/> záměrně — čeká na frontu, sestavení a CDN, které tento repozitář nevlastní, a kontrola závislá na cizí latenci je kontrola, která se přeskakuje — ale <t6>pomalé</t6> a <t7>selhalo</t7> jsou různé skutečnosti a ta druhá má API. <t8/> ji čte na jednom místě pro oba volající: <t9/> shodí běh při chybě sestavení v okamžiku, kdy nastane, a <t10/> se na totéž ptá potom týmž příkazem. en: A version is a semantic version: three numbers, an optional pre-release part and optional build metadata (<t1/>), ordered by semantic-version precedence — <t2/>, build metadata ignored. A pre-release is only ever an explicit target (<t3/>); nothing derives one. Raising a pre-release lands on the final it leads up to (<t4/> raised by a major, a minor or a patch is <t5/>), and a pre-release of the floor reaches it (<t6/>): with a floor of <t7/>, <t8/> is accepted, so an alpha series can continue, while nothing goes below a version already declared. The last release a plan measures from is the highest recorded version, a pre-release included; the stable pointer (<t9/>) never is one.

Pre-release je vždy jen explicitní cíl (<t3/>); žádný se neodvozuje. Zvýšení pre-release přistane na finální verzi, k níž vede (<t4/> zvýšená o major, minor či patch je <t5/>), a pre-release spodní meze ji dosáhne (<t6/>): se spodní mezí <t7/> se přijímá <t8/>, takže řada alfa může pokračovat, zatímco nic nejde pod už deklarovanou verzi.
